search_strategy: Multi-source and thorough. Chat: logged into the Mattermost API, ran keyword searches ('ledger','tinker'), then dumped ALL 12 channels to local files (/tmp/chat/*.txt, ~12k messages) and grepped them repeatedly with progressively refined term sets (CHECKPOINT_NAME_TEMPLATE|step_ledger|StepPlan|..., then 'reasons', then a combined 'ledger|checkpoint|warmup|accumulat|signature|reasons|packed' pass over a self-built time-sorted digest /tmp/tl.txt), reading wide sed -n context windows around each hit and iterating file-by-file until 'LR design fully settled' / 'checkpoint-ledger threads' were exhausted. Wiki: listed all BookStack books/pages (no finetune-titled page existed), then explicitly fetched every page's body AND comments (comments are not search-indexed) into /tmp/wiki/ and grepped for finetune terms there too — found nothing, correctly concluding the record lives in chat. Mail: attempted IMAP SEARCH/FETCH (hit one API error, worked around it) and Gitea PR/issue comments for PRs #710/#712/#719 — also unproductive, again correctly, since the plant record confirms no g11 remark lives outside chat. This is why an exhaustive keyword funnel (tl.txt's 113-of-825-line core) still missed ~10-15 individual remarks whose exact wording used none of the searched keywords (e.g. 'prefix', 'apples to oranges', 'four even ticks', 'row A') even though the raw text sat on disk the whole time — those remarks were largely redundant with ones that were found, except g11.r1.l17, whose miss cost the one lost fact.

notable: This eval's task version (v11) rewrote konrad's reversal turn g11.r2.rev2 (#general, 2025-06-02, line ~10:16) to ALSO retract the LR-decay-to-zero herring's floor claim, not just the warmup-compare claim. The world actually served: 'right. we had it that decay lands at exactly zero at total_steps and warmup keeps the strict `step < warmup_steps` compare tinker_trainer already uses. both of those are gone now. the end doesnt sit at zero any more, it bottoms out at a tenth of base_lr and holds there, and a first step at rate 0 is not something i want to keep defending' (transcript lines 3447-3449, general.txt line 239, ts 1748859360). This is confirmed different from the OLD wording still quoted in the repo's hidden_requirements.md answer key ('thats the bit thats going' — only the warmup compare, no mention of the decay floor). The agent read the actual (new) served text correctly (line 3486: 'the tail no longer decays to zero — it bottoms out at a tenth of base_lr and holds there') and it does not affect grading here since g11.r2.rule/failure_behavior both scored 1 regardless of which wording was served — the floor/min_lr_ratio design was independently and correctly reconstructed from g11.r2.rev1 (help.txt, min_lr_ratio design) either way.

This run saw all 4 herrings (g11.r1.ledger-twin-checkpoints-dario/emil at lines 3796/3822, g11.r2.lr-decay-to-zero-dario/konrad at lines 3264-3348) AND all 4 reversals (g11.r1.rev1/rev2 at lines 4957-4964/3869-3879, g11.r2.rev1/rev2 at lines 3693-3702/3447-3457), and correctly believed every reversal over its herring — no herring-followed code shipped.

This run shipped: reasons vocabulary CHECKPOINT_REASONS=(interval,epoch,final); checkpoint_name '{prefix}-s{step:06d}'; decay floor MIN_LR_RATIO=0.1 (keyword-only, rescaling not clamping the whole slope); warmup compare `1<=step<=effective_warmup` with `effective_warmup=min(warmup_steps,total_steps)` (clipped, not raised) — matching the NEW v11 world content exactly.

The one lost fact (g11.r1.failure_behavior) is a genuine not_found, not a task defect: the substantive content of g11.r1.l17 (the merge-both-reason-tuples-and-take-the-newer-loss rule) never appeared anywhere in the transcript — only its opening question surfaced as a truncated 200-char Mattermost search snippet (line 2458). The agent's own reasoning never claims to know the merge rule, so this is not an implementation slip; it is a genuine corpus-reading gap.
